extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing submissions to the Journal of Machine Learning Research (machine learning researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to JMLR, including scope, originality, formatting, cover letter contents, review process, and publication terms. Targeted at machine-learning researchers intending to submit papers to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — acceptable topics and types of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR seeks previously unpublished papers on machine learning that contain: new principled algorithms with sound empirical validation, and with justification of theoretical, psychological, or biological nature; experimental and/or theoretical studies yielding new insight into the design and behavior of learning in intelligent systems; accounts of applications of existing techniques that shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of the methods; formalization of new learning tasks (e.g., in the context of new applications) and of methods for assessing performance on those tasks; development of new analytical frameworks that advance theoretical studies of practical learning methods; computational models of data from natural learning systems at the behavioral or neural level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list defines the kinds of contributions JMLR publishes; occasional surveys are by invitation from the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness, completeness, and polish
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be concise and complete; manuscripts should be carefully proofread and polished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that do not meet these criteria may be returned unreviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for claims — experiments or theory and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims should be clearly articulated and supported either by empirical experiments or theoretical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, authors are encouraged to implement their work and to demonstrate its utility on significant problems; any experiments reported should be reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems papers — describe contributions and underlying principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers describing systems should clearly describe the contributions or the principles underlying the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe what the system contributes beyond implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical papers — discuss practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers describing theoretical results should also discuss their practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear how theoretical results affect practice or understanding of learning systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance and significance — show how the work advances understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, it should be clear how the work advances the current state of understanding and why the advance matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should report on what was learned in doing the work, rather than merely on what was done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature context and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must clearly acknowledge the contributions of their predecessors, and situate their submission in the context of the broader machine learning research literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper introduces new terminology or techniques, it should also explain why current terminology or techniques are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality — prior publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to JMLR cannot have been published previously in any other journal. JMLR will consider submissions that have been published at workshops or conferences, but expects the JMLR submission to cite the prior work, go into much greater depth and to extend the published results in a substantive way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must notify JMLR about previous publication at the time of submission, attach the previous paper as a supplementary document, and explain the differences from their prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: JMLR will consider concurrent submissions of papers that are under review at conferences, provided the conference explicitly allows for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide their conference submission to the JMLR action editor; differences between the papers must satisfy the same substantive-extension requirements as for prior publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable and insufficient deltas from conference versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable 'deltas' include new theoretical results, entirely new application domains, significant new insights and/or analyses. Insufficient deltas include adding proofs omitted from a conference paper; minor variations or extensions of previous experiments; adding extra background material or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision about whether a 'delta' is significant enough is ultimately left to individual reviewers (and the AE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit work to JMLR that is already available as a preprint, for example on arXiv or personal websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirement — JMLR LaTeX style and PDF-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be typeset in LaTeX using the JMLR LaTeX style file. Only PDF files should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers not in the JMLR style file will be rejected without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online appendices and supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles may be accompanied by online appendices containing data, demonstrations, instructions for obtaining source code, or the source code itself if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly encouraged to include such appendices. Note: if an online appendix contains source code, authors will be required to sign a release form prior to publication freeing JMLR from liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code encouragement and repository recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to provide electronic forms of applicable data sets or executable code and to submit data sets to the UCI Machine Learning Repository where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including data and code increases reproducibility and utility of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Though there are no explicit page limits, papers longer than 50pp will take a longer time to review and may be desk rejected if an AE and reviewers cannot be found to handle it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep manuscripts concise where possible to avoid longer review delays or possible desk rejection for manageability reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required cover letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles must be accompanied by a cover letter (in PDF or plain text) containing: disclosure of any previous publications by the author(s) that significantly overlap with the submission (describe differences); confirmation that all co-authors are aware of and consent to the submission; declaration of possible conflicts of interest (name all action editors recently collaborated with); suggestions of 3 to 5 action editors (from the Action Editors list) and 3 to 5 reviewers (no conflicts of interest); list of keywords from the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing multiple AE and reviewer suggestions helps expedite handling; do not suggest conflicted reviewers (e.g., advisee/advisor relationship is a lifelong conflict).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical submission checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a paper, prepare it in PDF format (if multiple files, create an archive), prepare the cover letter as described, ensure uploaded file is less than 5Mb, and ensure title page contains required items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the submission steps at http://jmlr.org/manudb and confirm receipt via the manuscript listing; the manuscript ID tag and status will be shown there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must contain complete name, post and e-mail address of the corresponding author; a condensed running title of fifty (50) characters or less; a list of five key-words; an abstract that does not exceed 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are required metadata fields for submission; ensure correct formatting per the authors guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to look at Joelle Pineau's useful checklist about reproducibility in machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow best practices for experiment reporting and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-in-Chief initial screening and desk rejection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a paper is submitted to JMLR, it is scanned by the Editor-in-Chief (EIC). If the EIC finds that the paper is very clearly below the standards of the journal, or not in its scope, or if there are no suitable action editors, then the paper can be rejected without written review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scope, quality, and format are adequate before submission to avoid desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Editor assignment and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIC assigns the paper to an action editor (AE) who has expertise in the area of the paper. If the AE finds that the paper is very likely to be rejected on full review, the AE will write a single short review explaining that position, and the paper will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AE decides on reviewers, may desk-reject with a short review, and makes the final decision based on reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment and review expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The AE assigns the paper to three reviewers. The reviewers write detailed technical reviews of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one review arrives in reasonable time, and that review is detailed and of high quality and recommends rejection and the AE agrees, the AE may decide to reject the paper. If two reviews come in and the decision is clear, the AE may accept or reject, or wait for the third review or commission additional reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible editorial decisions and post-decision actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible decisions are Accept and Reject. Accepted papers may still require minor revisions, usually checked only by the action editor. Rejection may or may not be accompanied by encouragement to resubmit. Papers that are rejected will fall into two categories: those that are permitted to be resubmitted and those that are not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should obtain explicit permission from an action editor before resubmitting a paper; permission for resubmission is not a guarantee of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timeline expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: After initial submission, an action editor will be assigned within about one month. The AE will then pick 3 reviewers who may take 1-3 months to review. The AE makes the final decision, which will usually be available within 4-6 months after initial submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some papers may take longer (e.g., very long/complex papers or during busy conference review periods); a few may take less time (e.g., if rejected without review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication license and copyright policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a paper is accepted, authors must sign an agreement granting a CC-by license to the public, which allows for publication in JMLR online by JMLR, Inc. and in a print-archive edition by Microtome Publishing. The copyright remains with the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be prepared to sign the CC-by agreement upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance materials and linking policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to provide electronic forms of any applicable data sets or executable code. They are also encouraged to add links to the article and the JMLR site to their personal web pages; if the authors wish to create a page pointing to subsequent related research, JMLR will maintain a link from the original paper to this page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the authors guide for a detailed checklist of post-acceptance actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fees policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no publication fees associated with this journal and all papers are freely available to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting resources and common errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are provided links to an authors guide, reviewers guide, instructions for formatting JMLR articles, common formatting errors, annotated sample JMLR paper and style file, permission to publish form (PDF), and software release form (PDF) to be sent if executable code is made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these resources (e.g., http://www.jmlr.org/format/authors-guide.html) to ensure correct formatting and to avoid common errors that may cause rejection or delays.
